title: Normalization predicate for the existing derived tensor pullback comparison
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ and $(D,K)$ be sites essentially small in a coefficient universe $r$, let $R$ and $S$ be sheaves of commutative rings, and use their module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and ordinary unbounded derived categories with independent localization universes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the already constructed derived tensor $T_R,T_S$ and resolving comparison $\rho_{P,Q}:Q\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\cong T_R(QP,QQ)$ of [def-sf-ringed-kflat-tensor-representative-data]; the names canonicalDerivedTensor and canonicalRepresentativeIso denote exactly these existing data. For a ringed pullback presentation $f$, its termwise pullback $f^*$ and canonical insertion-of-one total comparison $c_{P,Q}$ [def-pur-cochain-tensor-coherence-data], a functor $L:D(R)\to D(S)$ and a natural transformation $\epsilon:Q_R L\to f^*Q_S$ (where composition is read left to right), define $\Phi_L=T_R\mathbin{\gg}L$ and $\Psi_L=(L\times L)\mathbin{\gg}T_S$. For any natural transformation $\tau:\Phi_L\to\Psi_L$, define IsNormalized to mean: for every pair of K-flat complexes $P,Q$ with flat terms, their pullbacks are K-flat with flat terms, and, using those witnesses for the target resolving comparison,
$$L(\rho_{P,Q})\,\tau_{(Q_RP,Q_RQ)}\,T_S(\epsilon_P,\epsilon_Q)=\epsilon_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)}\,Q_S(c_{P,Q})\,\rho_{f^*P,f^*Q}.$$
This is a predicate on the supplied transformation, not an assertion that such a transformation exists, is unique or is invertible. No shift structure or exactness hypothesis on $L$ is included.
